Subject: Orbit: Hosted API residency + retention questionnaire

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the NDA. We're working through procurement and need some specific answers for our security questionnaire focused on data residency, retention and deletion for the hosted API. Attached is our filled RFI (orbit_security_questionnaire.pdf) — the sections we care most about are:

- Can we require region lock to US-only?
- How long are prompts & responses persisted by default, and what controls do customers have to shorten that?
- What is the deletion workflow and SLA for tenant data and backups?
- Are cached prefixes / KV caches persisted beyond the immediate session?

Would appreciate consolidated answers we can add to our RFP package. If helpful, happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Best,
Jae
Senior InfoSec Manager
Orbit Analytics

Hi Jae — thanks for sending this. We've looped in Kim (security), Ben (account lead) and Marissa (platform) to make sure answers are complete and include operational details for procurement.

Quick summary up front: yes, we support US-only region pinning for hosted API customers (policy + technical controls), default persistence is short-lived telemetry and cached artifacts are ephemeral by default, and we provide auditable deletion workflows with defined SLAs — details below from Kim and Marissa.

I've attached an internal matrix (residency_matrix.csv) that maps request types to storage scopes. Please let us know any follow-ups — we can also offer a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Security & Trust | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jae Park <jae.park@orbitanalytics.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Orbit: Hosted API residency + retention questionnaire

Hi Jae / Liam — thanks for the clear RFI. Below are concise, procurement-friendly answers you can paste into your questionnaire. I included operational notes and links to evidence where applicable.

1) Region lock (US-only)
- Yes. Customers on our hosted plan can request region pinning to US data centers. We enforce this in the control plane routing and tenant placement at onboarding.
- Enforcement: requests from your tenant are routed to US-hosted inference pools; logs and backups for the tenant are stored in US regions only unless you authorize otherwise.
- Controls: region is set as a tenant attribute and can be validated via API and during SOC/assessment review.

2) Default persistence for prompts & responses
- Default: for standard hosted API customers, prompt and model response payloads are retained for 24 hours for immediate debugging, telemetry aggregation, and billing reconciliation.
- Shortening: customers may opt into a reduced retention policy at onboarding (e.g., 0-hour transit-only — no persistent storage except ephemeral caches) via a tenant setting. This is a contractual option for customers with strict data minimization needs.

3) Deletion workflow & SLA
- Tenant-level deletion flow:
  a. Customer submits deletion request via Console API / Support ticket.
  b. Control plane schedules deletion job which removes tenant blobs, indexed records, and cache entries.
  c. Snapshots/backups containing tenant data are flagged for secure deletion and purged according to the backup retention window.
- SLA: primary data purged from live stores within 72 hours of confirmed request; backup snapshots removed within 30 days (we can shorten this in contract for enterprise customers with escrow arrangements).
- Evidence & audit: deletion jobs are logged and an audit record is generated; we can provide deletion attestations for covered customers.

4) Caching and KV prefix behavior
- Prefix KV caches are kept in-memory and short-lived by default; they are not persisted to long-term storage unless explicitly configured for a specific tenant.
- Ephemerality: intra-request KV and prefix caches are cleared on model session termination; optional short-lived cache replication (for multi-request flows) is available but is configurable and documented in the tenant settings.

5) Encryption, key management & access controls
- All data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. Keys are managed in our KMS; enterprise customers may bring their own keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations.
- Access: Production inference hosts do not allow interactive administrative access; operator actions are audited.

6) Backups & replication
- Backups are region-tagged. Cross-region replication is off by default for region-pinned tenants.
- Retention: standard backup retention is 30 days; enterprise addendum can reduce or extend this window.

7) Evidence & attachments
- We've included a residency_matrix.csv mapping each artifact type (request logs, model traces, KV caches, backups) to storage scope and retention.
- For procurement: we can produce an export of audit logs showing deletion jobs and a redactable attestation.

If you need formal language for the questionnaire (Q/A with short answers), I can provide a two-column CSV. Also happy to take clarifying questions during a quick call.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security PM | Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim — that level of detail is perfect. Two follow-ups from procurement:

1) The 24-hour default window: can you provide a short statement we can show legal/ops that confirms 24 hours is standard for non-enterprise tenants?
2) Deletion SLA: we need to understand how "flagged for secure deletion" maps to backups that are encrypted and potentially stored for 30 days — can you confirm whether the backup deletion is a hard delete or crypto-shred, and whether we get an attestation when job completes?

Also attaching our completed RFI with line numbers for ease of reference. Would like to take the 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow if someone from your side can do 11:00am PT.

Thanks,
Jae

Attachment: orbit_security_questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Jae / Liam — Ben here (account). Appreciate the clear questions and thanks Kim for the answers.

We can do 11:00am PT tomorrow for a 30-minute walkthrough — confirming tentative invite sent to your calendar. On the two clarifications:

- 24-hour default statement: Kimberly will provide a short, copy-ready sentence for procurement; we can also include it in the order form as a standard description for non-enterprise tenants.
